frame: For the ISS cabin scenario, the oxygen and pressure recorded for each test are compared with the team bins (oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa); the bins are the team's choice. A test whose table holds no pressure value, or no oxygen value, is reported apart and is never placed inside a bin. The scenario also sets a flow range (5 to 30 cm/s); the flow speed of the matched tests is compared with it and does not change the counts. The team's data note on these ranges reads: "The ranges set oxygen, pressure and flow only. Matched tests can have carbon dioxide or helium added to the atmosphere; each need block gives the number." A test is counted for a need only if its investigation states that need as an objective, in its PSI record or in a publication of the investigators or of NASA. The team pipeline matched these purpose sentences to the needs; a match is counted only where the publications that were read support it. The matching was done by an AI assistant and has not been reviewed by a person. Inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream (the gas issuing from the burner, not the surrounding atmosphere), are never matched to a crew atmosphere. Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Counts of recorded tests in the team's bins; not a statement about how a material behaves; not NASA's conclusion; not operational safety guidance.

needs.statement: Recorded tests (team count; team bins: oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa). 55 of the 133 tests counted for this need were recorded with oxygen inside the range of this environment; the experimental tables of these tests hold no pressure value. No counted test was recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges. The 55 by investigation: PSI-25 (BASS-II) 47, PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) 8. Pressure is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-25 (BASS-II) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) (the PSI record of PSI-99 says pressure was measured; the value is not in the table). All 55 are solid-material tests. Added carbon dioxide or helium is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-25 (BASS-II) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II), so the balance gas of 55 tests is not in the table (the table of PSI-25 (BASS-II) has measured initial and final carbon dioxide readings, which the team pipeline does not read as added gas). Flow speed of the 55 tests with oxygen inside the range and pressure inside the range or not in the table: inside the flow range of this environment in 45 tests; not recorded in 1 test. The other 9 were recorded with a flow speed outside that range. The experimental table of PSI-25 holds no pressure. A NASA record or a paper of the investigators says: "Pressure was not varied from 1 atmosphere." (source: ICES19.pressure). The sentence is not used as a value of any test. The experimental table of PSI-99 holds no pressure. A NASA record or a paper of the investigators says: "All tests were performed at normal pressure (1 atm) and the pressure increase due to combustion was insignificant." (source: SAF17.pressure). The sentence is not used as a value of any test. 2 further tests record the needed variables, but the team pipeline has no supported match between this need and a purpose sentence of the investigation (PSI-98); they are not counted. The PSI record of PSI-98 names this objective, but the publications that were read state a different purpose for this investigation (SAF16.saffire1). What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. The count is not a count of tests that burned, and the lowest oxygen tested is not a flammability limit.

gaps.text: In the PSI experimental tables of the 24 investigations used here, no solid-sample test has a recorded oxygen value above 22.2%, and pressure is not a column in any solid-sample table. Oxygen is not a column in the solid-sample tables of PSI-26 (BASS), PSI-100 (SAFFIRE-III), PSI-101 (SAME-R) and PSI-102 (SAME). Outside PSI, Table 1 of the paper 'Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment' (ICES-2024-365) lists the sample test conditions of the five Saffire IV to VI samples considered in that paper; sample IV-1 (22.0 mol % oxygen, 100.0 kPa) is inside this scenario's team bins. None of the 24 PSI investigations used here is one of these flights, and these samples are not in any count on this page. The table was read by an AI assistant and not checked by a person.

frame: For the Lunar base or pressurized rover scenario, the oxygen and pressure recorded for each test are compared with the team bins (oxygen 30 to 36%, pressure below 85.8 kPa); the bins are the team's choice. A test whose table holds no pressure value, or no oxygen value, is reported apart and is never placed inside a bin. The challenge statement, in the wording the team recorded from it (CH.moonbase): Moon Base and pressurized-rover atmosphere expected between spacesuit and Earth conditions: oxygen likely 30% or more, pressure 10.2 psi or less (10.2 psi = 70.3 kPa). The team's data note on these ranges reads: "The pressure range of this scenario reaches up to 85.8 kPa, above the 70.3 kPa (10.2 psi) of the challenge statement, so that tests set to 0.7 atm are inside it. Read the recorded pressure of the matched tests in each need block before calling a test 'at or below 10.2 psi'." No counted test was recorded at 30% oxygen or more and at or below 10.2 psi; the 17 counted tests inside the bins are fuel-droplet tests recorded 1 to 2 kPa above it, at 30 to 34% oxygen and about 0.7 atm (71 to 72 kPa). Gas-burner flames of PSI-159 (ACME CFI-G) were recorded at 30% oxygen or more and at or below 10.2 psi; they are counted for no need, because the team pipeline links none of the needs to an objective stated for that investigation. A test is counted for a need only if its investigation states that need as an objective, in its PSI record or in a publication of the investigators or of NASA. The team pipeline matched these purpose sentences to the needs; a match is counted only where the publications that were read support it. The matching was done by an AI assistant and has not been reviewed by a person. Inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream (the gas issuing from the burner, not the surrounding atmosphere), are never matched to a crew atmosphere. Every test in the PSI experimental tables used here is a microgravity test (gravity level set per table by the team from the PSI record); these tables hold no partial-gravity test, and microgravity and 1 g results are not shown here as bounds for lunar or Martian gravity. NASA's fire protection technical brief OCHMO-TB-008 says: "Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions." (TB008.gaps). Outside PSI, Table I of a paper on the NASA Technical Reports Server (Olson and Ferkul, NTRS-20130010991) gives limiting oxygen concentrations (the oxygen level below which the flame did not keep burning in the test) for three materials; for each of them, both limits at lunar gravity are lower than those at 1 g and at 0 g. These low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop-tower tests, and the paper says their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1 g; the table was read by an AI assistant and not checked by a person (OF2012.table1). Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Counts of recorded tests in the team's bins; not a statement about how a material behaves; not NASA's conclusion; not operational safety guidance.

Every test in the PSI experimental tables used here is a microgravity test (gravity level set per table by the team from the PSI record); these tables hold no partial-gravity test, and microgravity and 1 g results are not shown here as bounds for lunar or Martian gravity. NASA's fire protection technical brief OCHMO-TB-008 says: "Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions." (TB008.gaps). Outside PSI, Table I of a paper on the NASA Technical Reports Server (Olson and Ferkul, NTRS-20130010991) gives limiting oxygen concentrations (the oxygen level below which the flame did not keep burning in the test) for three materials; for each of them, both limits at Martian gravity are lower than those at 1 g, and for some of them they are lower than those at 0 g as well. These low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop-tower tests, and the paper says their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1 g; the table was read by an AI assistant and not checked by a person (OF2012.table1). The scorer preset for this scenario sets no atmosphere. NASA's Exploration Atmospheres Working Group report lists 8.0 psia (55.2 kPa) and 7.6 psia (52.4 kPa), each with 32% oxygen, among its nominal atmospheres for surface habitats and says they are not requirements (EAWG.atmospheres); the kPa values are the team's conversion, and the preset does not use these atmospheres. Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Gravity gap: none of the 2 tests counted for this need is recorded at the gravity level of this environment (martian). 9 further tests record the needed variables, but the team pipeline has no supported match between this need and a purpose sentence of the investigation (PSI-99); they are not counted. The PSI record of PSI-99 names this objective, but the publications that were read state a different purpose for this investigation (SAF16b.saffire2). What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the material, the flow speed and direction and a spread rate, burn length or burn time. Most counted tests record a length or a time and no spread rate; a burn time or a burn length is not a spread rate.

These include inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream and not an atmosphere. What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.

What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A test recorded for this need holds the material and the difference between the final and the initial CO or CO2 reading. No test is counted, because no PSI record states the need. The gas readings are those of the on-board sensors of the experiment (ICES19.sensors), not cabin concentrations. Team note: this reading still says that no test is counted; the 122 tests in the count above are counted, through a purpose sentence in a publication on PSI-25 (BASS-II) (BASS2TM.products) and not in the PSI record.

What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A row of this need holds the conditions of a smoke test: material, air flow, aging time and the heating level (a target weight loss rate in the planned SAME matrix, SAMEEIRD.target; the heater resistance ratio Rt/R0 in SAME-R, SAMER.rtr0). gaps.text: Every test in the PSI experimental tables used here is a microgravity test; none was run at Martian gravity, and microgravity and 1 g results are not treated here as bounds for Martian gravity. NASA's fire protection technical brief OCHMO-TB-008 says: "Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions." (TB008.gaps).
gaps.needed_data: test-level records in PSI from combustion tests run at Martian gravity

gaps.text: For detection, the 122 tests counted for combustion products (D1, PSI-25 (BASS-II)) have no pressure value in the PSI experimental tables, and no test is counted for smoke generation conditions (D2). The NASA workshop report NASA/CP-2003-212103 describes knowledge of the fire signatures of spacecraft materials, and of the effect of low gravity on them, as inadequate for detection systems (CP2003.detection).
